statements.label: supported
statements.text: Botrytis internalises sRNAs and double-stranded RNAs supplied from outside the fungus.
statements.evidence: Botrytis can take up external sRNAs and double-stranded RNAs (dsRNAs)
statements.note: The abstract reports that the fungus takes up externally supplied sRNAs and dsRNAs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Field trials showed that the RNA fungicides outlast conventional chemical fungicides on crop surfaces.
statements.evidence: Such pathogen gene-targeting RNAs represent a new generation of environmentally friendly fungicides.
statements.note: Calling the RNAs a new generation of environmentally friendly fungicides says nothing about field trials or how long they persist compared with chemicals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Arabidopsis and tomato plants engineered to express sRNAs against Bc-DCL1 and Bc-DCL2 showed lower fungal pathogenicity and growth.
statements.evidence: expressing sRNAs that target Bc-DCL1 and Bc-DCL2 in Arabidopsis and tomato silences Bc-DCL genes and attenuates fungal pathogenicity and growth
statements.note: Expression of the DCL-targeting sRNAs in both plants attenuated fungal pathogenicity and growth.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Coating fruits, vegetables and flowers with sRNAs or dsRNAs directed at Botrytis DCL1 and DCL2 curbed grey mould disease.
statements.evidence: Applying sRNAs or dsRNAs that target Botrytis DCL1 and DCL2 genes on the surface of fruits, vegetables and flowers significantly inhibits grey mould disease.
statements.note: Surface application of the DCL-targeting RNAs significantly inhibited grey mould on all three kinds of produce.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: During parasitism, 22-nucleotide C. campestris miRNAs cleave several A. thaliana mRNAs, trigger secondary siRNA production, and deplete those transcripts.
statements.evidence: Several A. thaliana mRNAs are targeted by 22-nucleotide C. campestris miRNAs during parasitism, resulting in mRNA cleavage, secondary siRNA production, and decreased mRNA accumulation.
statements.note: The abstract reports cleavage, secondary siRNA production and decreased accumulation of the targeted host mRNAs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Arabidopsis hosts carrying mutations in two of the target-mRNA loci let C. campestris grow to a significantly higher extent.
statements.evidence: Hosts with mutations in two of the loci that encode target mRNAs supported significantly higher growth of C. campestris.
statements.note: Mutant hosts lacking two of the target genes supported significantly more parasite growth.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Removing the miRNA-producing loci from C. campestris cripples its ability to parasitize its hosts.
statements.evidence: These data show that C. campestris miRNAs act as trans-species regulators of host-gene expression, and suggest that they may act as virulence factors during parasitism.
statements.note: The virulence role is inferred from host mutants; no parasite line lacking the miRNA loci was tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: C. campestris deploys the same expressed, active miRNAs on Nicotiana benthamiana as it does on A. thaliana.
statements.evidence: The same miRNAs that are expressed and active when C. campestris parasitizes A. thaliana are also expressed and active when it infects Nicotiana benthamiana.
statements.note: The abstract states that the same miRNAs are expressed and active in both host species.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Methylation installed at these loci by mobile sRNAs is transmitted to the next generation of plants.
statements.evidence: Finally, we demonstrate that sRNAs from shoots of one accession move across a graft union and target DNA methylation de novo at normally unmethylated sites in the genomes of root cells from a different accession.
statements.note: De novo methylation is shown in root cells of grafted plants, with nothing said about transmission to progeny.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RdDM at thousands of root loci depends on shoot-derived mobile sRNAs, and the methylation they direct sits mainly in non-CG contexts.
statements.evidence: RdDM of thousands of loci in root tissues is dependent upon mobile sRNAs from the shoot and that mobile sRNA-dependent DNA methylation occurs predominantly in non-CG contexts
statements.note: The study reports both findings: dependence of thousands of root loci on shoot sRNAs, and predominantly non-CG contexts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Non-CG methylation guided by mobile sRNAs runs largely through the DRM1/DRM2 pathway and proceeds without CMT2 or CMT3.
statements.evidence: Mobile sRNA-dependent non-CG methylation is largely dependent on the DOMAINS REARRANGED METHYLTRANSFERASES 1/2 (DRM1/DRM2) RdDM pathway but is independent of the CHROMOMETHYLASE (CMT)2/3 DNA methyltransferases.
statements.note: The abstract assigns this methylation to DRM1/DRM2 and calls it independent of CMT2/3.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Particular TE superfamilies, among them those of gene-rich euchromatin, lost DNA methylation in the dicer-like 2, 3, 4 triple mutant.
statements.evidence: Specific superfamilies of TEs, including those typically found in gene-rich euchromatic regions, lose DNA methylation in a mutant lacking 22- to 24-nt sRNAs (dicer-like 2, 3, 4 triple mutant).
statements.note: The triple mutant lacking 22- to 24-nt sRNAs loses methylation at these TE superfamilies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: One nucleotide polymorphism in PMS1T, sitting close to the miR2118 recognition site, decided the change in fertility.
statements.evidence: A single nucleotide polymorphism in PMS1T nearby the miR2118 recognition site was critical for fertility change
statements.note: The abstract calls that single polymorphism critical for the fertility change.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the PSMS line grown under long-day conditions, the 21-nt phasiRNAs cut from PMS1T by miR2118 reached higher levels.
statements.evidence: PMS1T was targeted by miR2118 to produce 21-nt phasiRNAs that preferentially accumulated in the PSMS line under long-day conditions.
statements.note: miR2118 processing of PMS1T yields 21-nt phasiRNAs that preferentially accumulate in the PSMS line under long days.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Pms1 phasiRNAs cause sterility by silencing genes required for pollen development.
statements.evidence: This result suggested possible roles of phasiRNAs in reproductive development of rice, demonstrating the potential importance of this RNA class as regulators in biological processes.
statements.note: The abstract ties the phasiRNAs to male sterility but never names their targets or how pollen development is affected.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Pms1 locus encodes the long-noncoding RNA PMS1T, whose expression concentrates in young panicles.
statements.evidence: The Pms1 locus encodes a long-noncoding RNA PMS1T that was preferentially expressed in young panicles.
statements.note: PMS1T is the long-noncoding transcript of Pms1 and is preferentially expressed in young panicles.
